# Turning Poultry Challenges into Performance Gains in Nigeria


14 September 2026 in:


[Animal Nutrition & Health](https://www.iff.com/category/animal-nutrition-health/)


*How a practical, data-led nutrition approach helped one poultry producer address real production pressures*


Across Africa, poultry production sits at the center of a much bigger story. **It** supports food security, creates livelihoods, and helps supply affordable protein to growing communities.


Feed costs remain a major pressure. Raw material quality can vary. Heat stress can disrupt flock performance. Intestinal health challenges can affect productivity. At the same time, many operations are looking for practical ways to manage antibiotic use while keeping birds healthy and production consistent.


In practice, these challenges are not abstract. They show up in feed mills, layer houses, breeder operations, veterinary decisions, and daily business planning. For poultry producers in Nigeria, South Africa, and across the continent, the question is often simple: how do we protect performance when so many variables are moving at once?


For one integrated poultry producer in Nigeria, however, that question became urgent.


The operation included commercial layers, breeder production, and feed milling. It was already a significant player in the market, with more than 280,000 commercial layers, 10,000 layer breeders, and an annual feed volume of 25,000 metric tons. The business produced eggs and day-old chicks for Nigeria and neighboring countries, while also planning further capacity expansion.


But scale did not remove the pressure. The operation was dealing with high feed costs, inconsistent feed quality, intestinal disorders, heat stress, high mortality, and egg quality concerns. These issues were affecting performance and limiting the producer’s ability to compete as efficiently as possible.

##


Starting with the farm, not the formula


Rather than begin with a product-first answer, the IFF Animal Nutrition & Health team started with diagnosis. The team looked at the feed, the production environment, the health challenges, and the economics behind the operation.


Specifically, that included reviewing feed formulation and raw material quality, assessing soybean meal quality through trypsin inhibitor analysis, and using laboratory analysis of fecal samples to better understand the intestinal health challenge. The team also conducted a controlled field trial with 10,000 layers over 60 days.


This mattered because the producer was not facing one isolated issue. Feed cost, nutrient availability, intestinal balance, heat stress, mortality, and egg quality were connected. A narrow response may have addressed part of the problem. Instead, the operation needed a more integrated view.


IFF’s nutribiotic approach became relevant here. Nutribiosis is the interaction between nutrition, the microbiome, and gut and immune function. IFF’s approach focuses on these interactions to support livestock production, including during under challenging conditions.


##


Building a nutritional-health strategy


The team recommended a combined nutritional-health program using Axtra C010T, Enviva® PRO, and Betafin®. The approach brought together enzyme technology, probiotic support, and natural betaine as part of one program tailored to the farm’s conditions.


Each element had a role.


Technology
Purpose in this case


Enzyme technology Supporting nutrient release across key parts of the diet


Probiotic support Contributing to the gut-health strategy


Natural betaine Supporting birds under heat and performance pressure


The enzyme component **addresses** nutrient release across key parts of the diet. The case material notes xylanase for fiber digestion, amylase for starch, protease for protein digestibility, and phytase activity to help release phosphorus bound by phytate.


The probiotic component,[Enviva® PRO](https://www.iff.com/animal-nutrition/products/enviva-pro/) , anchors the gut health strategy. IFF describes Enviva® PRO as a three-strain Bacillus probiotic selected from the poultry environment and designed to support gut balance.


The betaine component,[Betafin®](https://www.iff.com/animal-nutrition/products/betafin/) , helps support birds facing heat stress and performance pressure. The case material specifically links Betafin® to managing heat stress challenges and overall bird performance in this operation. The result was not a one-size-fits-all recommendation. It was a practical program built around local feed realities, the producer’s production goals, and the technical evidence gathered before and during the trial.


##


What changed in this case


Indicator Before During/after the case trial


Egg production 82% 88.5%


Mortality 3.2% 0.6%


Daily feed per bird 120 g 115 g


Egg size Under 60 g 62–65 g


Annual feed cost $3.5M $3.2M


Under the conditions of this specific customer trial, the producer saw measurable changes across several performance and economic indicators.


Egg production increased from 82% to 88.5%. Mortality decreased from 3.2% to 0.6%. Daily feed quantity per bird decreased from 120 grams to 115 grams. Egg size moved from less than 60 grams to a range of 62 to 65 grams. Annual feed cost decreased from $3.5 million to $3.2 million. The case also reported a reduction in antibiotic cost from $5 million to $1 million, shown in the customer value table.


The total savings shown for the customer in the case material was $2.45 million, compared with $0.153 million for the competing solution. The same case summary also noted that relationship, trust, tenacity, and problem-solving were “immeasurably valuable” in the outcome.


That last point matters. The numbers tell one part of the story. But the way the work happened also matters. The team collaborated with the customer’s veterinarians, nutritionists, managing director, and purchasing team. They connected technical analysis with day-to-day production realities. They looked at the business impact and the biological challenge together.


For producers across Africa, that is often where progress starts. Not with a generic promise. Not with an imported answer. But with the right questions, the right data, and a team willing to work through the complexity.


The numbers tell one part of the story. The way the team worked through the complexity tells the other.


##


Why this story matters beyond one farm


Of course, no two farms are the same. Feed ingredients, climate, housing, disease pressure, management practices, and commercial goals can differ widely between Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ethiopia, and other African markets. Results from one operation should not be treated as a guarantee for another.


But this case does show something important: when poultry challenges are connected, the response should be connected too.


IFF’s poultry solutions are designed to address production challenges across stages of poultry production, including egg production, nutrition, liveability, and profitability. The IFF poultry page also lists enzyme, probiotic, combined technology, betaine, and essential oil solutions as part of the poultry portfolio.


For African poultry producers navigating feed cost pressure, raw material variation, heat stress, and changing expectations around antibiotic use, that kind of integrated support can help make technical decisions clearer. It gives teams a way to move from symptoms to root causes. From isolated interventions to a structured plan. From uncertainty to better-informed action.


##


A practical path forward


The poultry sector across Africa has enormous potential. But potential alone does not solve daily production challenges. Producers need practical tools, technical partnership, and solutions that respect local conditions.


As a result, this Nigerian case points to a grounded path forward. Start with the operation’s real pressures. Test assumptions with data. Understand what is happening in the feed and in the bird. Build a program that fits the farm, not just the brochure. Then measure what changes.


Ultimately, that is how science becomes useful. It moves from the lab into the feed mill, the layer house, the breeder operation, and the business conversation.


For poultry producers working to improve consistency, manage cost pressure, and strengthen flock resilience, the next step does not have to be complicated. It can begin with a conversation about what is happening on the farm today, and what a better path forward could look like.
